title: Build a Voice Assistant Pipeline — The Phase 6 Capstone
service: VoiceBot: tool dispatch, a SQLite session store, the voice tool loop and per-turn latency reports for a cascaded voice assistant

parts.lesson_anchor: Build It, Step 4 dispatch and code/main.py dispatch_tool; Pitfalls: No tool-call error handling, TTS that blocks
planted_bugs: parse_arguments decodes OpenAI-style JSON text but returns the original string; the AttributeError surfaces one call later in check_arguments, after a substring match fooled the required check
ToolError from _lookup and parse_arguments escapes dispatch, so an unknown tool or broken JSON ends the turn instead of going back to the LLM

JSON_TYPES is keyed 'int' while the schemas say 'integer', so integer parameters go unchecked; '300' reaches Timers.set_timer and comes back as a TypeError result without the parameter name, two calls from the root cause
plain-function tools run on the event loop, so a 2 s blocking weather lookup stalls the loop that also runs the microphone, VAD and barge-in detection
parts.timing_assert: longest event-loop stall during a 2 s blocking tool under 0.2 s (the blocking version stalls 2.0 s; the worker-thread version about 5 ms; on a loaded machine 169 of 170 runs stayed under 20 ms and one reached 39 ms)
parts.overfix_guard: async tools are still awaited (sending every tool to a worker thread returns an unawaited coroutine), and a tool that raises still comes back as an error result (narrowing the catch-all lets ConnectionError end the turn)

failure_modes.first-word clip: not testable from transcripts and event traces without the audio; a Part 4 follow-up asks for the fix (start threshold 0.3, 200-400 ms pre-roll). Capture and VAD are exercised in lessons 11 and 14
failure_modes.mid-response interrupt confusion: Part 4: barge_in_ms measures how long the assistant kept talking after user.barge_in; turn 3 stops at the barge-in (0 ms) and turn 4 is an uncancelled LLM talking over the user for 900 ms
failure_modes.silence hallucination: Part 4: a turn with no vad.start is reported as a hallucination, and a real 'Thank you.' must stay a turn, so text filters fail

deviations: Part 1: dispatch is async because the lesson's pipeline is asyncio, and the timing assertion measures how long a blocking tool stalls the event loop (the lesson's 'TTS that blocks' pitfall) instead of a throughput loop. Besides the suggested guard (tool errors come back as results), a second guard keeps async tools awaited.
Part 2: session expiry is an idle TTL counted from the last message, and deletion must clear the bytes from the file, for the lesson's 'Logging PII forever' pitfall.
Part 3: adds the lesson's 'retry once, then gracefully degrade' rule and requires every tool call to be answered, alongside the suggested step limit and speakable text.

Part 4: events carry a turn id; vad.start, vad.end and turn.end join the suggested event types; out-of-order arrival is bounded by max_delay_ms and handled with a watermark; reports are server-sent events, since 06/03 already uses NDJSON.
Part 5: the schema is a voice routine whose steps nest through a recursive $ref, with type lists and RFC 6901 pointer escaping.
